A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D visual grounding framework, renamed from EaSe to LASP. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Nr3D, ScanRefer and Sr3D evaluations, code-generation ablations, and additional quantitative and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original grounding and ablation results and adds GRScenes evaluation, a human-written encoder comparison and a viewpoint analysis.

M1.justification: After matching the main text and appendices, semantic parsing, relation encoders, recursive execution, test-guided code optimization and VLM candidate selection retain the same procedures. Renaming and additional code illustrations do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v4 removes the ScanRefer evaluation and adds transfer evaluation on GRScenes using 40 annotated expressions across five scenes. This introduces unseen environments with supplied object boxes and categories while removing the detection-based ScanRefer setting. Nr3D and Sr3D coverage remains.

E2.justification: The Nr3D comparison adds SAT, SeeGround and CSVG; the cost comparison adds SeeGround and CSVG. v4 also introduces a random baseline for GRScenes and a human-written encoder comparison. NS3D remains in the appendix, and ViL3DRel/ViL3DRef denotes the same retained comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include a matched-VLM LASP/SeeGround comparison, human-function substitution, a 100-sentence viewpoint analysis, and GRScenes evaluation with supplied boxes and categories. v4 specifies GPT-4o results for Transcrib3D and revises the stated test-suite size from under 50 to under 100 cases for most relations. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds analyses of human-written versus generated encoders, cross-dataset transfer, and viewpoint-anchor alignment, plus a front-encoder refinement case study. The original optimization ablations, condition-level accuracy analysis, relation-constraint examples and unit-test/generalization plots are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, statistical error bars or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Nr3D headline accuracies of 52.9% and 67.8% remain, but v4 fills in subgroup scores and adds GRScenes results of 90.0% versus 15.6% random, 44.0% with human-written encoders, and matched-VLM results of 48.8% versus SeeGround's 40.7%. ScanRefer results are removed. Transcrib3D's reported overall score changes from 70.2% to 65.6% in the newly specified GPT-4o comparison, not a demonstrated same-setting decline. The NS3D subset baseline changes from 52.8% to 52.7%.

T1.justification: Category and relation feature definitions, product-based execution, and symmetry/asymmetry properties are retained across relocation and notation changes. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central code-based grounding contribution and accuracy-efficiency claim remain. v4 narrows the headline benchmark claim to Nr3D, explicitly allows a small optimization dataset within its definition of training-free, and adds introductory claims about transfer and advantages over human-designed encoders.

C2.justification: v1's brief limitations expand into substantive discussion of ordinal expressions, omitted rare relations, scene representation, atomic test suites and dependence on pretrained perception models. v4 also adds interpretations of implicit viewpoint assumptions, cross-dataset transfer and amortized code-generation costs.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses RTX 4090 hardware, per-relation optimization and API-token cost information, and public-resource links and licenses; it also changes the advertised code repository. Existing prompts and principal hyperparameters remain. ScanRefer implementation details and the Near-code listing are removed.

R1.justification: v4 expands discussion of CSVG and SeeGround, both already cited in v1, and adds works including SAT, SORT3D and perception-model research. Several broader neuro-symbolic references are removed. The fundamental positioning against agents, visual programming and learned relation encoders remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten, and the paper and method are renamed. Technical explanations are consolidated into Appendix B, while dedicated Limitations, Ethics Statement and public-resource sections substantially reorganize the document.

P2.justification: Overview diagrams are redesigned, and v4 adds a VLM image montage, a front-code illustration and GRScenes displays. The above-code comparison becomes a colored code diff, the Nr3D table gains explicit comparison groups, and figures and algorithms are extensively rearranged. The ScanRefer table is removed.

improvement.justification: Clearer disclosure of small-sample supervision and pretrained perception dependencies, expanded limitations, and new encoder and matched-VLM comparisons improve transparency and support for the central argument. The gains are tempered by removal of ScanRefer evidence, the small 40-expression transfer study, and numerical inconsistencies such as Transcrib3D's 50.3k tokens in v4's prose versus 12k in Table 2.
